@updates.failure.check.description: Shown in the menu-triggered update-check toast and in the status line of Settings > Updates & privacy when a check for a new version didn't get an answer. {reason} is one or two complete, already-translated sentences saying why and what to do (for example "Cmdr couldn't reach its server. Check your internet connection and try again."), so end your sentence with a period and let the reason follow it. "Cmdr" is the product name (do not translate). Avoid the words "error" and "failed".

placeholders.reason: one or two already-translated sentences saying why the check didn't get an answer and what to do; Cmdr controls the wording but the length varies

@updates.failure.check.screenshotNote: App-update messaging. The status line renders in the Settings > Updates & privacy panel pictured here, and the update toasts appear while that check runs. Version numbers are substituted, not translated.

updates.failure.checkUntyped: Cmdr couldn’t check for updates. Check your internet connection and try again later.

@updates.failure.checkUntyped.description: Same place as updates.failure.check, used when Cmdr can't tell why the check didn't get an answer (usually the internet connection). Two sentences: what didn't happen, then what to try. "Cmdr" is the product name (do not translate). Avoid the words "error" and "failed".
@updates.failure.checkUntyped.screenshotNote: App-update messaging. The status line renders in the Settings > Updates & privacy panel pictured here, and the update toasts appear while that check runs. Version numbers are substituted, not translated.

updates.failure.download: Cmdr couldn’t download the update. Try again later.

@updates.failure.download.description: Shown in the update-check toast and in Settings > Updates & privacy when a new version was found but downloading it didn't finish. Nothing was installed, and the current version keeps working. "Cmdr" is the product name (do not translate). Avoid the words "error" and "failed".
@updates.failure.download.screenshotNote: App-update messaging. The status line renders in the Settings > Updates & privacy panel pictured here, and the update toasts appear while that check runs. Version numbers are substituted, not translated.

updates.failure.install: Cmdr couldn’t install the update. Try again later, or get the latest Cmdr from getcmdr.com.

@updates.failure.install.description: Shown in the update-check toast and in Settings > Updates & privacy when a new version was downloaded but writing it into the app didn't finish. Points at the website as the fallback. "Cmdr" is the product name and "getcmdr.com" the website address: keep both exactly as-is. Avoid the words "error" and "failed".
@updates.failure.install.screenshotNote: App-update messaging. The status line renders in the Settings > Updates & privacy panel pictured here, and the update toasts appear while that check runs. Version numbers are substituted, not translated.

@updates.checkToast.sendErrorReport.description: Button in the update-check toast that opens the error-report flow after a failed update check. Tight mini button.
@updates.checkToast.sendErrorReport.screenshotNote: App-update messaging. The status line renders in the Settings > Updates & privacy panel pictured here, and the update toasts appear while that check runs. Version numbers are substituted, not translated.

updates.toast.ready: A new version of Cmdr is ready.

@updates.toast.ready.description: Headline of the persistent toast that appears once an update has been downloaded and written into the app. It states the situation; the line below it says what happens next. Sentence case.
@updates.toast.ready.screenshotNote: App-update messaging. The status line renders in the Settings > Updates & privacy panel pictured here, and the update toasts appear while that check runs. Version numbers are substituted, not translated.

updates.toast.readyDetail: Restart now, or you’ll get it the next time you open Cmdr.

@updates.toast.readyDetail.description: Second line of the update-ready toast, under the headline. Reassures the user that doing nothing still gets them the new version: the update is already written to disk and only needs a fresh launch to take effect. Conversational, and the point it has to land is that no action is required.
@updates.toast.readyDetail.screenshotNote: App-update messaging. The status line renders in the Settings > Updates & privacy panel pictured here, and the update toasts appear while that check runs. Version numbers are substituted, not translated.

@updates.toast.versionChange.description: Small, dimmed metadata line at the bottom of the update-ready toast, showing which version replaces which. Version numbers and an arrow only, with no words to translate; the literal "v" prefix and the arrow are both intentional. Keep it identical to English unless your language writes version numbers differently.

placeholders.prev: the version the user is running right now (for example 0.28.3)
placeholders.next: the version that has been downloaded and will run after a restart (for example 0.29.0)

@updates.toast.versionChange.screenshotNote: App-update messaging. The status line renders in the Settings > Updates & privacy panel pictured here, and the update toasts appear while that check runs. Version numbers are substituted, not translated.

@updates.toast.versionChangeAria.description: Accessible name for the version line above, which a screen reader would otherwise read out as a bare arrow symbol. Never visible on screen. A plain sentence naming both versions.

placeholders.prev: the version the user is running right now (for example 0.28.3)
placeholders.next: the version that has been downloaded and will run after a restart (for example 0.29.0)

@updates.toast.versionChangeAria.screenshotNote: App-update messaging. The status line renders in the Settings > Updates & privacy panel pictured here, and the update toasts appear while that check runs. Version numbers are substituted, not translated.

@updates.toast.later.description: Button that dismisses the update-available toast without restarting now. Tight mini button.
@updates.toast.later.screenshotNote: App-update messaging. The status line renders in the Settings > Updates & privacy panel pictured here, and the update toasts appear while that check runs. Version numbers are substituted, not translated.

@updates.toast.restart.description: Button that restarts the app immediately so the already-downloaded update takes effect. Paired with a "Later" button that dismisses the toast. Tight mini button, so keep it short.
@updates.toast.restart.screenshotNote: App-update messaging. The status line renders in the Settings > Updates & privacy panel pictured here, and the update toasts appear while that check runs. Version numbers are substituted, not translated.

updates.moveToApplicationsDialog.title: Move Cmdr to your Applications folder

@updates.moveToApplicationsDialog.title.description: Title of the dialog shown when a new version is available but Cmdr is running from somewhere it can't update itself. Sentence case. "Applications" is the macOS folder name, which Apple localizes per system language.

updates.moveToApplicationsDialog.translo: A new version is ready, but macOS is running Cmdr from a temporary read-only copy of itself. That’s what happens when you open an app straight from where you downloaded it, and it means updates have nowhere to land.

@updates.moveToApplicationsDialog.transl.description: First paragraph of the move-to-Applications dialog, for the macOS App Translocation case (the app was opened from the Downloads folder). Explains why the update can't be applied. Conversational.

updates.moveToApplicationsDialog.readOnl: A new version is ready, but Cmdr is running from a read-only spot, usually a disk image that’s still mounted. That means updates have nowhere to land.

@updates.moveToApplicationsDialog.readOn.description: First paragraph of the move-to-Applications dialog, for the case where the app runs from a read-only volume such as a mounted .dmg disk image. Conversational.

updates.moveToApplicationsDialog.howTo: Quit Cmdr, drag it into your Applications folder, and open it from there. Every update after that arrives on its own.

@updates.moveToApplicationsDialog.howTo.description: Second paragraph of the move-to-Applications dialog: the instruction the user should follow. "Applications" is the macOS folder name, which Apple localizes per system language.

@updates.moveToApplicationsDialog.gotIt.description: The only button in the move-to-Applications dialog; closes it. Short, friendly acknowledgement.
